conditions: Right triangle in Euclidean geometry; c is the hypotenuse.
spoken_aliases: a squared plus b squared equals c squared

evidence: Place four congruent right triangles of legs a,b inside a square of side a+b so their hypotenuses form the boundary of a central square of side c. The central angles are right angles because the acute angles of each triangle are complementary. Comparing areas gives (a+b)^2=4(ab/2)+c^2, hence a^2+b^2=c^2.

Reference cross-check of the standard relationship: https://openstax.org/books/intermediate-algebra-2e/pages/11-1-distance-and-midpoint-formulas-circles. Checked 2026-11-27. Proposed maintainer approval; not independent human certification.
